Taxpayers below the no-tax threshold owe no income tax and need no credit; the personal credit reduces the income tax for low-to-moderate income filers just above that threshold.

_strings.@@27ffd534203d: Connecticut Earned Income Tax Credit (CT EITC) — Connecticut full-year residents who claimed and were allowed the 2023 federal Earned Income Credit. Taxpayer (and spouse/qualifying children, if applicable) must have valid Social Security Numbers by the return due date, must have earned income from employment or self-employment, and must meet all federal EITC rules. Either qualify with a qualifying child, or as a worker without a qualifying child aged 25-64.

_strings.@@a97bea97e800: Treaty conformity — CT does NOT conform to federal tax treaties: income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is STILL taxable by CT. Do not carry a federal treaty exclusion onto the state return. (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state's Internal Revenue Code conformity date and its deduction/credit conformity are separate questions; see any law-change lines below.) State note: CT's resident return (Form CT-1040) starts from federal AGI (Line 1 = "Federal adjusted gross income from federal Form 1040, Line 11"), so treaty-exempt income is initially excluded. HOWEVER, CT has an EXPLICIT ADD-BACK: the 2023 CT-1040 instructions (Schedule 1 additions, Line 37 "Other") and the 2023 CT-1040NR/PY instructions (Schedule 1 additions, Line 39 "Other") both direct: "1. Add back any treaty income reported on federal Form 1040NR if a nonresident alien. Enter the words 'treaty income' in the space provided." Because CT requires nonresident aliens to add federally treaty-exempt income back into Connecticut adjusted gross income, CT does NOT conform to federal treaty exemptions for affected filers (analogous to California's Schedule CA add-back). Note: this add-back is scoped to nonresident aliens filing federal Form 1040NR; a filer with no treaty income / not a nonresident alien is unaffected, but the statutory rule re-taxes treaty income, so conforms_to_federal_treaties = false.
_strings.@@c0e7931c928a: Credit for Income Taxes Paid to Qualifying Jurisdictions (Schedule 2) — Connecticut residents (and part-year residents) whose income reported on the CT return is also subject to income tax in another qualifying jurisdiction (another U.S. state, a local jurisdiction within another state, or the District of Columbia) where the taxpayer filed a return and paid income tax. Prevents double taxation of the same income. A copy of the other jurisdiction's return must be attached.
_strings.@@c2a03ce984ef: Property Tax Credit (Schedule 3) — Connecticut residents who paid qualifying property tax during 2023 to a Connecticut political subdivision on their primary residence and/or a privately owned or leased motor vehicle. Single/MFS/HOH limited to one motor vehicle; MFJ/qualifying surviving spouse limited to two. (For 2023 there is no longer an age-65-or-dependent eligibility restriction; the credit is available to any resident who paid qualifying property tax.) Cannot be claimed if Form CT-1040 Line 10 is zero.

state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: 2023 Form CT-1040, Line 6: 'Income Tax'. Computed on the Tax Calculation Schedule (2023 CT-1040 instructions, p. 19): Line 1 = Connecticut AGI (Form CT-1040, Line 5); Line 2 = Table A personal exemption; Line 3 = Connecticut Taxable Income (Line 1 - Line 2, not less than zero); Line 4 = Table B Initial Tax Calculation (the rate schedules this block ships); Lines 5-6 add Table C (3% phase-out) and Table D (recapture); Line 8-9 subtract the Table E personal-credit percentage; Line 10 'Connecticut Income Tax: Subtract Line 9 from Line 7. Enter here and on Form CT-1040, Line 6.' This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Base guidance: supply Tax Calculation Schedule Line 3 (Connecticut Taxable Income) = Connecticut AGI (Form CT-1040 Line 5 = federal AGI + Schedule 1 additions - Schedule 1 subtractions) MINUS the Table A personal exemption. The Table A exemption (up to $15,000 single / $24,000 MFJ-QSS / $12,000 MFS / $19,000 HoH) is INCOME-DEPENDENT — it falls $1,000 for each $1,000 (or part) of CT AGI over $30,000 / $48,000 / $24,000 / $38,000 and is $0 at CT AGI of $44,000 / $71,000 / $35,000 / $56,000 or more — so it is NOT shipped as a key; compute Table A on the form. At or above the zero point, Line 3 = CT AGI. Do NOT supply raw federal AGI when CT modifications apply, and do NOT subtract the exemption twice. Adjudication note (two-pass): drafted from the 2023 CT-1040 instructions (Rev. 12/23) Tables A-E and independently re-verified against the 2023 CT-1040NR/PY instructions (Rev. 12/23) — identical tables, zero discrepancies. Every printed '$X plus Y% of the excess over $Z' constant in Table B equals the EXACT cumulative sum of the prior brackets (300/2,300/5,050/11,050/14,300/31,550 single-MFS; 600/4,600/10,100/22,100/28,600/63,100 MFJ; 480/3,680/8,080/17,680/22,880/50,480 HoH), so pure marginal accumulation reproduces Table B to the half-dollar; the only divergence is IRS half-up rounding of a trailing $.50 (e.g. the DRS's own printed examples $33,298 at single $525,000 and $52,228 at HoH $825,000 round 25,000 x .0699 = $1,747.50 up). CRITICAL — Table C 3% Tax Rate Phase-Out Add-Back NOT modeled: if CT AGI (Tax Calculation Schedule Line 1, NOT taxable income) exceeds $56,500 single / $100,500 MFJ-QSS / $50,250 MFS / $78,500 HoH, Line 5 ADDS BACK $20-to-$200 (single/MFS, max above $101,500/$72,750), $40-to-$400 (MFJ, max above $145,500), or $32-to-$320 (HoH, max above $114,500), clawing back the benefit of the 3% bottom rate. Plain bracket math (this op) UNDERSTATES the filed tax by the Table C amount — compute Line 5 on the form. CRITICAL — Table D Tax Recapture NOT modeled: if CT AGI exceeds $200,000 single/MFS / $400,000 MFJ-QSS / $320,000 HoH, Line 6 adds a recapture amount rising in steps ($90/$180/$140 per band) to a plateau of $2,700/$5,400/$4,200, then a second phase above $500,000/$1,000,000/$800,000 CT AGI to the maximum $3,150 (single/MFS, CT AGI over $540,000), $6,300 (MFJ, over $1,080,000), $4,920 (HoH, over $864,000). Plain bracket math understates the filed tax by the Table D amount at those AGI levels — CT's Tax Calculation Schedule is the filed method. Table E Personal Tax Credits NOT modeled (a TAX CREDIT, not a base reduction): a CT-AGI-keyed decimal (.75 down to .01) multiplies the Line 7 tax and is subtracted on Line 9 for low/moderate incomes — e.g. .75 for single CT AGI $15,000-$18,800 — fully phased out above CT AGI $64,500 single / $100,500 MFJ-QSS / $52,500 MFS / $78,500 HoH. No-tax floor (2023 CT-1040 instructions, Line 6): if CT AGI (Line 5) is $12,000 or less MFS / $15,000 or less single / $19,000 or less HoH / $24,000 or less MFJ-QSS, enter '0' on Line 6 — no income tax is owed. This coincides with the full Table A exemption at those AGI levels (the engine's max(0, ...) floor matches). Tax tables are OPTIONAL, not mandated: at CT AGI of $102,000 or less the filer 'may' use the DRS website Tax Tables (portal.ct.gov/DRS/DRS-Forms/Current-Year-Forms/Calculators-and-Tables); the Tax Calculation Schedule is the universal filed method at any income (table bands can differ from schedule arithmetic by a few dollars). One Table B schedule covers 'Single or Married Filing Separately' — duplicated for both statuses here, copied, not derived (Table A/C/E amounts DO differ between single and MFS). The MFJ schedule is titled 'Married Filing Jointly/Qualifying Surviving Spouse', so qualifying surviving spouse maps exactly to married_filing_jointly as the engine assumes. Connecticut has no county or municipal income taxes and no standard deduction; the Table A personal exemption and the personal credit are the only general-relief mechanisms, both income-dependent, both computed on the Tax Calculation Schedule.
